title: 'The Murders in the Rue Morgue,' by Edgar Allen Poe, Part One (3/3)
titleZh: 愛倫坡《莫爾格街兇殺案》第一部分 (3/3)
summaryZh: 杜邦說中了敘事者心裡的想法，讓他察覺對方驚人的推理能力。
source: VOA Learning English (public domain) — American Stories

sentences.text: One who coldly put things together, and another who just as coldly took them apart.
sentences.zh: 一個人冷靜地把事情拼湊起來，另一個人同樣冷靜地把它們拆解開來。

sentences.text: One night, we were walking down one of Paris' long, dirty streets.
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上，我們走在巴黎一條又長又髒的街上。

sentences.text: We were quiet, both busy with our own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我們都沒說話，各自想著自己的心事。

sentences.text: He is a very little fellow, that's true, and he would be more successful if he acted in lighter, less serious plays.
sentences.zh: 他確實是個矮小的傢伙，這是真的，如果他去演比較輕鬆、不那麼嚴肅的戲，應該會更成功。

sentences.text: Yes, there can be no doubt of that, I said.
sentences.zh: 我說：「對，這一點毫無疑問。」

sentences.text: At first, I saw nothing strange in this.
sentences.zh: 一開始，我並不覺得這有什麼奇怪。

sentences.text: This, of course, seemed to me quite natural.
sentences.zh: 當然，這在我看來再自然不過。

sentences.text: Dupin had not agreed with something I had said.
sentences.zh: 杜邦同意的並不是我說出口的話。

sentences.text: He had agreed directly with my thoughts.
sentences.zh: 他直接同意的是我心裡的想法。

sentences.text: I had not spoken a word.
